name: MovieCat
subtitle: Your movie & TV file library
promotionalText: Point MovieCat at your movie folders and instantly see posters, ratings and summaries for every film and show. No account or API key needed.
whatsNew: New: woke ratings from WokeGauge. Titles that wokegauge.com has reviewed show their rating (0–10) on the poster and in the details, with a spoiler-free verdict and a link to the full review. Filter your library by rating band, and sort from least to most woke.
description:
MovieCat turns folders full of video files into a beautiful, browsable movie library.

Point it at your movie and TV folders and MovieCat recognises each title from its file name, even messy release names like "The.Matrix.1999.1080p.BluRay.x264". It then shows the poster, rating, year, genres, runtime and a short summary.

FEATURES
• Works instantly: no account, no sign-up, no API key
• Recognises movies and TV episodes from file names, including season/episode numbers and foreign titles
• Groups TV episodes by show
• Folders with a mix of content can show only recognised movies and shows, hiding home videos, screen recordings and tutorials
• Rate titles yourself with 1 to 10 stars
• Search, filter (Movies, TV, Unrecognised) and sort by title, year or rating
• Woke ratings from WokeGauge (wokegauge.com) for the titles it has reviewed: see the rating on the poster, filter by rating band and sort from least to most woke
• Fix a wrong match in seconds
• Play a file or show it in Finder with one click
• Optional free TMDB key for even better matching

PRIVATE BY DESIGN
MovieCat has no account and collects no data. Your library stays on your Mac; only titles are sent to public movie databases to look them up, and the IDs of recognised titles to WokeGauge for their ratings.

MovieCat is not affiliated with IMDb. TV data from TVmaze. This product uses the TMDB API but is not endorsed or certified by TMDB.
reviewNotes:
MovieCat organises the user's own video files; no login is needed.

How to test:
1. Launch and click "Get started" (the TMDB key is optional, skip it).
2. Click "Add folder" and choose a folder with video files. Empty placeholder files work, e.g. create files named "Big.Buck.Bunny.2008.mkv", "Sintel.2010.mkv" and "Night.of.the.Living.Dead.1968.mkv".
3. Titles are identified from the file names and shown with poster, rating and summary. Click a poster for details.
4. In the details, the trash buttons move a file, a season or all files of a title to the Trash after a confirmation. This is why the app asks for read-write access to folders the user picks.

Metadata comes from public services: IMDb search suggestions, Cinemeta and TVmaze. The red banner in the top-right corner links to our other app, ABCx3, on the Mac App Store.

WokeGauge: titles that wokegauge.com has reviewed show a woke rating (0–10, a gauge icon in the colour of its band) on the poster and in the details, with a one-sentence verdict and a link to the review. The "Woke" menu next to Sort filters by rating band, and Sort has least/most woke. To see ratings, add files named for reviewed films, e.g. "2.Guns.2013.mkv" and "After.the.Hunt.2025.mkv". MovieCat sends only the IMDb IDs of recognised titles to wokegauge.com; nothing is stored.
